idea.description: Add scalar context-dependent gates between short- and original-dilation causal convolution paths inside the supplied corrected NextItNet. Both paths are jointly trained components of one network, with exactly one independently trained model/checkpoint loaded per category. Interpret the mechanism as adaptive transformation weighting, not a guaranteed cutoff of older history.
idea.motivation: The user diagnosis identifies stale isolated interactions and broadly relevant recommendations displacing specific recent-purpose matches. Adaptive scale weighting explicitly targets both, although success requires behavioral evidence. Electronics' 12.27% sampled wrong-rank rate and negative tenth-percentile margin provide a model-facing target. These observations justify an experiment, not an expected HR@10 improvement. Uniform multi-negative softmax remains a simpler subsequent alternative if gating fails; changing both simultaneously would obscure attribution.
idea.implementation_notes:
Start from the supplied corrected NextItNet. Retain embeddings, hidden width, residual ordering, normalization, objective, optimizer, routing and sampling initially. Record the inherited configuration verbatim, including convolution variant, kernel sizes, dilation schedule, dropout and optimizer settings; these were not supplied in the report and must not be invented. Modify temporal convolutions with original dilation d>1: compute parallel dilation-1 and dilation-d paths with the same input/output dimensions and kernel size. Leave dilation-1 layers unchanged. Combine branch preactivations before the baseline's subsequent normalization/activation. Use a positionwise scalar sigmoid gate computed from the sublayer input, initialized with zero weights and bias -2, favoring the original path. Copy the baseline convolution initialization to the original path; initialize the added path with the baseline initialization rule. Train all parameters jointly. Do not combine independently fitted predictors.

Count every temporal convolution when documenting receptive fields: for stride-one layers, the maximum span is 1 + sum((k_l-1)*d_l); residual blocks may contain multiple convolutions, schedules accumulate across repetitions, and span does not guarantee every offset is reachable. A short branch operating on contextualized states still inherits their older dependencies. If strict bounded history is later tested, derive the branch from raw embeddings within each permitted window and bound its gates and bypasses as well; that is a separate architectural experiment.

Use explicit left padding of (k-1)*d with valid causal convolution, or verify equivalent baseline behavior. Apply channel-only LayerNorm to B×L×C; avoid training normalization that aggregates across timesteps. Keep the padding embedding zero and mask invalid positions after biased convolutions, affine normalization and residual updates before subsequent temporal mixing. Mask padded losses. Verify causality by perturbing future inputs and checking earlier features in deterministic evaluation mode. Test claimed dependency bounds by perturbing inputs outside those bounds. The proposed contextualized gate has no strict short-window invariance claim.

Preserve log2feats(sequence), item_emb and predict_score(features, items), including existing tensor conventions. For left padding, gather the largest nonzero-token index, normally L-1; never use count minus one. Preserve baseline handling of empty histories explicitly. Update the embedded predictor writer, checkpoint architecture configuration and state loading together. Verify that a freshly loaded generated predictor reproduces trained-model scores on identical inputs. Each category loads exactly one selected checkpoint.

Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Probe the actual view.model through ModelView using valid training positions from (None, sequence, positive, negative). Return measured metrics and definitions; retain margin diagnostics and optionally add gate entropy, saturation, branch gradients and gate dependence on history length. Unavailable category-based breakdowns must be marked unavailable, not fabricated. Only public histories, timestamps, item titles and descriptions are allowed; ratings, reviews, stores, prices, categories and simulator traits are unavailable. Title similarity cannot establish physical compatibility or replacement need.

Predeclare a small comparison matrix: corrected baseline, identical two-path network with fixed gate sigmoid(-2), and conditioned gate. Fixed and conditioned variants isolate adaptation with nearly identical capacity; disclose extra parameters relative to baseline, and use a matched-capacity ungated control only if budget permits. Gate freezing/permutation and inference-only suffix truncations are diagnostic interventions on the same fitted network. Retrained truncation controls, if affordable, are separate trials because inference-only truncation creates distribution shift. Record every attempted configuration and actual GPU time within the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget; do not promise a trial count without runtime evidence. Do not inspect other trials or reuse their checkpoints.

Keep preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, at most 200 epochs, exactly 200 batches per epoch, single-GPU execution, four-category routing, DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], and trial-local artifacts. Keep the host's 200 validation users/category, 99 unique negative candidates and evaluation seed 42 fixed. No test labels, evaluator changes, extra data or pretrained weights.

When host outputs expose per-user binary hits, bootstrap paired differences by resampling users within category and averaging the four category differences equally; report 95% intervals, category differences and discordant hit counts. Otherwise state that paired uncertainty is unavailable. One hit changes category HR by 0.5 percentage points and macro HR by 0.125 percentage points. Treat searched gains as exploratory; sampled margins and sampled HR do not establish full-catalog gains. User-facing benefits require the supplied qualitative assessment process, including separate tracking of uncertain identity and explicit mismatch. idea.pseudocode:
Record inherited baseline configuration, selection rule, comparison matrix and compute budget.
For each permitted configuration and each of the four categories:
    set the prescribed seeds; instantiate one corrected NextItNet
    preserve baseline sublayer ordering and objective
    for each original temporal convolution with dilation d > 1:
        replace its preactivation with:
            short = masked_causal_conv(input, dilation=1)
            original = masked_causal_conv(input, dilation=d)
            gate = sigmoid(positionwise_linear(input))
            mixed = gate * short + (1 - gate) * original
        continue baseline normalization, activation and residual processing
        reapply validity masks before further temporal mixing
    train jointly for at most 200 epochs, with 200 batches per epoch
    use unchanged next-item loss on valid positions
    preserve the predeclared baseline checkpoint-selection procedure
    save one selected model with complete architecture configuration
Select the configuration using unchanged host macro validation HR@10.
At prediction:
    load one selected model/checkpoint for the routed category
    compute log2feats(sequence)
    gather the largest nonpadding index, handling empty histories explicitly
    score candidates through predict_score(features, items)
Verify causality, padding behavior and generated-predictor score consistency.
Report measured margins and gate diagnostics separately from validation HR@10.
If available, compute paired user-level uncertainty; disclose selection bias.

idea_diagnosis.motivation: Qualitative feedback suggests older or isolated interactions may distract from coherent recent behavior, but does not establish current intent or satisfied needs. Cropping has established precedents, so the contribution is a controlled test of whether removing older accessible context improves this benchmark beyond changes in target weighting or supervision volume.
idea_diagnosis.implementation_notes: Use three predeclared conditions: A uses intact inputs and baseline supervision; B uses intact inputs with sampled suffix target masks; C uses the same masks as B and additionally removes older input context. In B/C, independently select rows with probability 0.25 and uniformly draw an integer retained length from 8 through 32, clipped to available nonpadding input length. For selected rows, retain original positions at or after the resulting cutoff; do not compact or shift. Preserve each retained target's original next-item alignment and immediate predecessor. Intersect the suffix mask with baseline valid-target positions. Generate B/C masks through a dedicated seeded augmentation RNG so augmentation does not change user, target or negative sampling; use matching initial weights, batch streams and optimizer steps. Use the identical baseline loss formula with explicit valid-target normalization; B/C must have identical denominators. Skip empty supervised batches consistently. A/B comparisons measure the combined effect of reduced and redistributed supervision, not a pure target-weighting effect. Each condition trains its own models from the supplied cold start; no checkpoints from other trials are reused, and no conditions are fused at inference. Bound this study by the remaining shared 43,200 GPU-second budget, counting controls, diagnostics and failures; defer optional all-position versus final-position comparisons if unaffordable. Before interpreting cropping, verify the baseline's actual dilation schedule, temporal convolutions, normalization axes, causality and padding behavior. Compute R = 1 + sum((kernel_width - 1) * dilation) over every stride-one temporal convolution; this describes accessible context only when other operations do not mix time globally. Leading-padding invariance requires preserving all real interactions and disabling dropout. For equal-length prefix interventions, changes strictly outside the receptive field should leave final features unchanged under position-local operations. Nonzero padded intermediate states can invalidate assumptions about replacing real prefixes with padding; audit them rather than assuming zero embeddings suffice. If padding fixes are necessary, apply them consistently to all conditions and update the embedded predictor. Evaluate intact left-padded histories at their final nonpadding position, normally L-1; never use nonpadding_count-1. Preserve splits, negative candidates, evaluator and checkpoint/predictor consistency. Select only by the prescribed macro validation HR@10. If the host exposes per-user validation hits, bootstrap paired user indices within each category and average four category differences equally; otherwise do not claim an interval. Predeclare configuration and checkpoint-selection rules and log every attempted condition. Intervals for selected winners do not correct validation-selection bias. idea_diagnosis.pseudocode:
conditions = ['A_full', 'B_mask_only', 'C_crop_and_mask']
# Run conditions separately from the supplied cold start; never fuse models.
for condition in conditions:
    reset_training_seed(42)
    model, optimizer = supplied_nextitnet_cold_start()
    batch_rng = dedicated_baseline_rng(seed=42)
    augmentation_rng = dedicated_augmentation_rng(seed=42)
    for step in prescribed_training_steps:
        sequence, positive, negative = baseline_sample_batch(batch_rng)
        valid = baseline_valid_target_mask(sequence, positive)
        suffix_mask = ones_like(valid)
        cropped_sequence = sequence.clone()
        # Generate the same augmentation schedule in every condition.
        for b in rows(sequence):
            occupied = nonzero_positions(sequence[b])
            crop_row = augmentation_rng.uniform() < 0.25
            if crop_row and len(occupied) > 0:
                s = min(augmentation_rng.randint_inclusive(8, 32), len(occupied))
                cutoff = occupied[-s]
                suffix_mask[b, :cutoff] = False
                cropped_sequence[b, :cutoff] = 0
        inputs = cropped_sequence if condition == 'C_crop_and_mask' else sequence
        supervised = valid if condition == 'A_full' else (valid & suffix_mask)
        if not supervised.any():
            continue
        features = model.log2feats(inputs)
        loss = baseline_loss_with_explicit_valid_normalization(
            features, positive, negative, supervised)
        optimizer.zero_grad()
        loss.backward()
        optimizer.step()
# B and C share target identities, negatives, masks and loss denominators.
# Evaluate every condition with intact histories and final-nonpadding readout.
# Host selection uses unchanged four-category macro validation HR@10.
# Each category predictor loads exactly one trained model/checkpoint.

report:
At 0% progress, prioritize a controlled experiment: **context-gated receptive fields within NextItNet**. Benefits remain hypotheses; no validation improvement has been measured.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Users reject broad relevance when recent behavior indicates a specific purpose, motivating adaptive context weighting. (2) Older, isolated interactions persist too strongly, motivating explicit tests of historical influence. (3) Electronics has 12.27% sampled ranking errors and a −0.2595 tenth-percentile margin, identifying confusing pairs without establishing validation HR@10. (4) Collapse scores of 0.5071–0.5234 imply near-zero average cosine similarity; global dispersion regularization has weaker diagnostic support.

**Insights from related work.** (1) [NextItNet](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.05163) supplies causal dilated residual convolutions, preserving the required family. (2) [Selective Kernel Networks](https://arxiv.org/abs/1903.06586) directly precedes input-conditioned scale selection, reducing originality claims; its evidence concerns images. (3) [MARS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.03718) motivates adaptive recency aggregation but uses a timestamp-aware post-encoder mechanism. (4) [ICSRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.14318) motivates subsequence intent supervision; [sampled-softmax analysis](https://wujcan.github.io/papers/tois-ssm.pdf) motivates stronger negative competition. Neither establishes gains here.

These insights define three directions: adaptive context scope, stronger ranking supervision, and subsequence consistency. The conceptual framework is:

| Direction | Mechanism | Diagnostic target | Main uncertainty |
|---|---|---|---|
| Context scope | Gate causal dilation paths | Stale interests; broad relevance | Contextualized paths retain older dependencies |
| Ranking supervision | Uniform multi-negative softmax | Weak lower-tail margins | Unobserved positives |
| Intent consistency | Match overlapping suffix representations | Unstable current preferences | May suppress genuine shifts |

**Candidate assessment.** Scores are prospective: O=originality, P=potential, U=user alignment, M=model alignment; higher D means harder implementation.

| Idea | O | P | U | M | D |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Gated receptive fields | 4 | 6 | 7 | 6 | 5 |
| Uniform multi-negative softmax | 2 | 6 | 4 | 9 | 2 |
| Suffix consistency auxiliary loss | 4 | 6 | 7 | 5 | 5 |

Gating offers adaptive weighting but has established precedents; user alignment is plausible but cannot establish compatibility; margin gains are unproven; implementation requires causal and predictor checks. def _read_split(path: str) -> dict[int, list[int]]:
    data: dict[int, list[int]] = defaultdict(list)
    if not os.path.isfile(path):
        return {}
    with open(path) as f:
        for line in f:
            parts = line.strip().split()
            if len(parts) == 2:
                data[int(parts[0])].append(int(parts[1]))
    return dict(data)


def _load_itemnum(data_dir: str, dataset_name: str) -> int:
    stats_path = os.path.join(data_dir, "dataset_stats.json")
    if os.path.isfile(stats_path):
        with open(stats_path) as f:
            stats = json.load(f)
        if dataset_name in stats:
            return int(stats[dataset_name]["itemnum"])
    itemnum = 0
    for split in ("train", "valid"):
        path = os.path.join(data_dir, f"{dataset_name}_{split}.txt")
        if not os.path.isfile(path):
            continue
        with open(path) as f:
            for line in f:
                parts = line.strip().split()
                if len(parts) == 2:
                    itemnum = max(itemnum, int(parts[1]))
    return itemnum


def load_dataset(dataset_name: str, data_dir: str):
    user_train = _read_split(os.path.join(data_dir, f"{dataset_name}_train.txt"))
    user_valid = _read_split(os.path.join(data_dir, f"{dataset_name}_valid.txt"))
    itemnum = _load_itemnum(data_dir, dataset_name)
    return user_train, user_valid, itemnum


def sample_batch(
    user_train: dict[int, list[int]], itemnum: int, batch_size: int, maxlen: int
):
    users = [u for u, items in user_train.items() if len(items) >= 2]
    if not users:
        raise RuntimeError("no users with at least two training interactions")
    batch_seq, batch_pos, batch_neg = [], [], []
    for _ in range(batch_size):
        user = random.choice(users)
        history = user_train[user]
        seq = np.zeros(maxlen, dtype=np.int64)
        pos = np.zeros(maxlen, dtype=np.int64)
        neg = np.zeros(maxlen, dtype=np.int64)
        nxt = history[-1]
        idx = maxlen - 1
        ### >>> Self_EvolveRec-BLOCK-START: Fail explicitly when negative sampling is impossible
        interacted = set(history)
        if len(interacted - {0}) >= itemnum:
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"User {user} has no unseen items available for negative sampling"
            )
        ### <<< Self_EvolveRec-BLOCK-END
        for item in reversed(history[:-1]):
            seq[idx] = item
            pos[idx] = nxt
            if nxt != 0:

                while neg_item in interacted:
                    neg_item = random.randint(1, itemnum)
                neg[idx] = neg_item
            nxt = item
            idx -= 1
            if idx < 0:
                break

        batch_pos.append(pos)
        batch_neg.append(neg)
    return np.asarray(batch_seq), np.asarray(batch_pos), np.asarray(batch_neg)


def _history_to_tensor(
    history: list[int], maxlen: int, device: torch.device
) -> torch.Tensor:
    seq_arr = np.zeros(maxlen, dtype=np.int64)
    for i, item in enumerate(reversed(history[-maxlen:])):
        seq_arr[maxlen - 1 - i] = item
    return torch.tensor([seq_arr], dtype=torch.long, device=device)


def evaluate_val(
    model: nn.Module,
    user_train: dict[int, list[int]],
    user_valid: dict[int, list[int]],
    itemnum: int,
    device: torch.device,
    maxlen: int,
    num_users: int = 200,
) -> dict[str, float]:
    val_users = [u for u in user_valid if u in user_train and user_valid[u]]
    if len(val_users) > num_users:
        rng = random.Random(SEED)
        val_users = rng.sample(val_users, num_users)
    if not val_users:
        return {"HR@10": 0.0, "HR@20": 0.0, "NDCG@10": 0.0, "NDCG@20": 0.0}

    hr10 = hr20 = ndcg10 = ndcg20 = 0.0
    model.eval()
    with torch.no_grad():
        for user in val_users:
            target = user_valid[user][0]
            history = user_train[user]
            interacted = set(history) | {target, 0}
            candidates = [target]
            while len(candidates) < 100 and itemnum > 0:
                neg_item = random.randint(1, itemnum)
                if neg_item not in interacted:
                    interacted.add(neg_item)
                    candidates.append(neg_item)
            seq_t = _history_to_tensor(history, maxlen, device)
            cand_t = torch.tensor(candidates, dtype=torch.long, device=device)
            scores = model.score_candidates(seq_t, cand_t).detach().cpu().tolist()
            rank = sorted(range(len(scores)), key=lambda i: -scores[i]).index(0)
            hr10 += 1.0 if rank < 10 else 0.0
            hr20 += 1.0 if rank < 20 else 0.0
            ndcg10 += (1.0 / math.log2(rank + 2)) if rank < 10 else 0.0
            ndcg20 += (1.0 / math.log2(rank + 2)) if rank < 20 else 0.0
    n = float(len(val_users))
    model.train()
    return {
        "HR@10": hr10 / n,
        "HR@20": hr20 / n,
        "NDCG@10": ndcg10 / n,
        "NDCG@20": ndcg20 / n,
    }


def bpr_sequence_loss(
    model: nn.Module, seq: torch.Tensor, pos: torch.Tensor, neg: torch.Tensor
) -> torch.Tensor:
    ### >>> Self_EvolveRec-BLOCK-START: Numerically stable BPR on valid training positions
    pos_scores, neg_scores = model(seq, pos, neg)
    valid = (seq != 0) & (pos != 0) & (neg != 0)
    margins = (pos_scores - neg_scores)[valid]
    return nn.functional.softplus(-margins).sum() / valid.sum().clamp(min=1)

class NextItNetBlock(nn.Module):
    def __init__(
        self, hidden_units: int, dilation: int, kernel_size: int, dropout_rate: float
    ):
        super().__init__()
        self.dilation = dilation
        self.kernel_size = kernel_size
        self.conv1 = nn.Conv1d(
            hidden_units, hidden_units, kernel_size, dilation=dilation, padding=0
        )
        self.conv2 = nn.Conv1d(
            hidden_units, hidden_units, kernel_size, dilation=dilation, padding=0
        )
        self.norm1 = nn.LayerNorm(hidden_units)
        self.norm2 = nn.LayerNorm(hidden_units)
        self.dropout = nn.Dropout(dropout_rate)
        self.activation = nn.GELU()
        if dilation > 1:
            # Conv1d's default initialization matches the original paths.
            self.short1 = nn.Conv1d(
                hidden_units, hidden_units, kernel_size, dilation=1, padding=0
            )
            self.short2 = nn.Conv1d(
                hidden_units, hidden_units, kernel_size, dilation=1, padding=0
            )
            self.gate1 = nn.Conv1d(hidden_units, 1, kernel_size=1)
            self.gate2 = nn.Conv1d(hidden_units, 1, kernel_size=1)
            for gate in (self.gate1, self.gate2):
                nn.init.zeros_(gate.weight)
                nn.init.constant_(gate.bias, -2.0)

    def _causal_conv(self, conv: nn.Conv1d, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        pad = (conv.kernel_size[0] - 1) * conv.dilation[0]
        return conv(nn.functional.pad(x, (pad, 0)))

    def _transform(self, index: int, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        original = self._causal_conv(getattr(self, f"conv{index}"), x)
        if self.dilation == 1:
            return original
        short = self._causal_conv(getattr(self, f"short{index}"), x)
        gate = torch.sigmoid(getattr(self, f"gate{index}")(x))
        # These paths transform contextualized states; neither guarantees a
        # strict cutoff of dependencies on older interactions.
        return gate * short + (1.0 - gate) * original

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor, mask: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        residual = x * mask
        y = (self.norm1(residual) * mask).transpose(1, 2)
        y = self._transform(1, y).transpose(1, 2) * mask
        y = self.dropout(self.activation(y)) * mask
        y = (self.norm2(y) * mask).transpose(1, 2)
        y = self._transform(2, y).transpose(1, 2) * mask
        y = self.dropout(y) * mask
        return (residual + y) * mask

class NextItNetModel(nn.Module):
    def __init__(
        self,
        itemnum: int,
        hidden_units: int = 64,
        num_blocks: int = 8,
        kernel_size: int = 3,
        dropout_rate: float = 0.2,
        maxlen: int = 128,
    ):
        super().__init__()
        self.itemnum = itemnum
        self.hidden_units = hidden_units
        self.maxlen = maxlen
        self.item_emb = nn.Embedding(itemnum + 1, hidden_units, padding_idx=0)
        self.pos_emb = nn.Embedding(maxlen + 1, hidden_units, padding_idx=0)
        dilations = [1, 2, 4, 8] * max(1, math.ceil(num_blocks / 4))
        self.blocks = nn.ModuleList(
            [
                NextItNetBlock(hidden_units, dilations[i], kernel_size, dropout_rate)
                for i in range(num_blocks)
            ]
        )
        self.dropout = nn.Dropout(dropout_rate)
        self.norm = nn.LayerNorm(hidden_units)
        with torch.no_grad():
            nn.init.xavier_uniform_(self.item_emb.weight)
            self.item_emb.weight[0].zero_()
            nn.init.xavier_uniform_(self.pos_emb.weight)
            self.pos_emb.weight[0].zero_()

    def encode_sequence(self, seq: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:

        pos = torch.arange(length, device=seq.device).unsqueeze(0).expand(batch, -1) + 1

        ### >>> Self_EvolveRec-BLOCK-START: Mask affine outputs before every temporal mixing operation
        mask = (seq != 0).unsqueeze(-1).to(self.item_emb.weight.dtype)
        x = self.item_emb(seq) * (self.hidden_units**0.5) + self.pos_emb(pos)
        x = self.dropout(x) * mask
        for block in self.blocks:
            x = block(x, mask)
        return self.norm(x) * mask
        ### <<< Self_EvolveRec-BLOCK-END

    def forward(self, seq: torch.Tensor, pos: torch.Tensor, neg: torch.Tensor):
        out = self.encode_sequence(seq)
        pos_scores = (out * self.item_emb(pos)).sum(dim=-1)
        neg_scores = (out * self.item_emb(neg)).sum(dim=-1)
        return pos_scores, neg_scores

    ### >>> Self_EvolveRec-BLOCK-START: Compatible feature scoring and explicit left-padded readout
    def log2feats(self, sequence: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        return self.encode_sequence(sequence)

    def predict_score(
        self, features: torch.Tensor, items: torch.Tensor
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        embeddings = self.item_emb(items)
        if features.shape[:-1] == items.shape:
            # Aligned next-item targets, including B x L training probes.
            return (features * embeddings).sum(dim=-1)
        # DEBUG: Support B x L x K candidates paired with B x L x H
        # features, returning B x L x K logits for sequence diagnostics.
        if items.ndim == features.ndim and items.shape[:-1] == features.shape[:-1]:
            return (features.unsqueeze(-2) * embeddings).sum(dim=-1)
        if items.ndim == 1:
            # A shared candidate list for each supplied feature vector.
            return torch.matmul(features, embeddings.transpose(0, 1))
        if features.ndim == 2 and items.ndim == 2:
            if features.size(0) != items.size(0):
                raise ValueError("Feature and candidate batch sizes differ")
            return (features.unsqueeze(1) * embeddings).sum(dim=-1)
        raise ValueError(
            f"Unsupported feature/item shapes: {features.shape}, {items.shape}"
        )

    def score_candidates(
        self, seq: torch.Tensor, candidates: torch.Tensor
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        out = self.log2feats(seq)
        positions = torch.arange(seq.size(1), device=seq.device).expand_as(seq)
        last = positions.masked_fill(seq == 0, -1).max(dim=1).values
        rows = torch.arange(seq.size(0), device=seq.device)
        user_emb = out[rows, last.clamp(min=0)]
        user_emb = user_emb * (last >= 0).unsqueeze(-1).to(user_emb.dtype)
        if candidates.ndim == 1:
            scores = torch.matmul(user_emb, self.item_emb(candidates).transpose(0, 1))

            scores = self.predict_score(user_emb, candidates)

        return scores[0] if seq.size(0) == 1 else scores

    print(f"predict.py written -> {predict_path}", flush=True)


def main() -> None:
    device = torch.device("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")
    print(f"Per-dataset NextItNet training on {device}", flush=True)
    scores = []
    for dataset_name in DATASETS:
        scores.append(train_one_dataset(dataset_name, device, DATA_DIR))
    working_dir = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "working")
    write_predict_script(working_dir)
    avg = sum(scores) / max(len(scores), 1)
    print(f"\nAll datasets done. Average val HR@10 = {avg:.4f}", flush=True)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

import torch

import torch.nn.functional as F

def diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis):
    return f"""
    You are a Senior AI Researcher analyzing the mathematical health of a Recommendation System.
    
    Here are the raw mathematical metrics measured from the current model:
    {json.dumps(raw_diagnosis['metrics'], indent=2)}
    
    Here are the definitions of what these metrics mean:
    {json.dumps(raw_diagnosis['metric_definitions'], indent=2)}
    
    Your task: produce a concise diagnosis summary that captures ONLY the core findings and implications.
    Do NOT propose web searches or action plans. Do NOT list "what to look up".

    Strictly follow the JSON format below.

    Output Format (JSON):
    {{
    "status": <CRITICAL | NEEDS_IMPROVEMENT | STABLE>,
    "core_findings": [
        "<1-2 sentences: the most important interpretation of the metrics>",
        "<1-2 sentences: the second most important interpretation (only if truly necessary)>"
    ],
    "key_implications": [
        "<1 sentence: what this implies about model behavior>",
        "<1 sentence: what this implies about training dynamics or representation>",
        "<optional 1 sentence: risk/trade-off if relevant>"
    ],
    "evidence": {{
        "headline_metrics": {{
        "<metric_name>": <value>,
        "<metric_name>": <value>
        }},
        "brief_metric_read": {{
        "<metric_name>": "<very short interpretation tied to its definition>",
        "<metric_name>": "<very short interpretation tied to its definition>"
        }}
    }}
    }}

    Rules:
    - Keep it short: core_findings <= 3 bullets, key_implications <= 3 bullets.
    - Use technical terms only when they are essential (e.g., 'gradient', 'loss landscape', 'inductive bias'), and keep them brief.
    - Every statement must be grounded in the provided metric values/definitions.
    - If metrics look healthy, status should remain STABLE and implications should focus on "what is already working" plus one potential risk to monitor.
    """


class DiagnosisProbe:
    def __init__(self, model, device):
        self.model = model
        self.device = device
        self.meta_data = model.meta_data
        self.review_data = model.review_data
        self.user_train = model.user_train

    def _get_categories(self, item_id: int):
        # DEBUG: Item categories are unavailable in this benchmark.
        # Keep the compatibility helper without inferring category labels.
        return []

    def analyze_embeddings_collapse_cosine(
        self, sample_size: int = 2048, seed: int = 42
    ):
        with torch.no_grad():
            emb = self.model.item_emb.weight.detach()
            emb = emb[
                1 : self.model.model.itemnum + 1
            ]  # exclude padding and reserved mask tokens

            n = emb.size(0)
            if n <= 2:
                return 0.0

            g = torch.Generator(device=emb.device)
            g.manual_seed(seed)

            k = min(sample_size, n)
            idx = torch.randperm(n, generator=g, device=emb.device)[:k]
            x = emb.index_select(0, idx)
            x = F.normalize(x, p=2, dim=-1)

            gram = x @ x.t()
            offdiag_sum = gram.sum() - gram.diag().sum()
            offdiag_cnt = k * (k - 1)
            mean_cos = (offdiag_sum / offdiag_cnt).clamp(-1, 1).item()

            collapse_score = (mean_cos + 1.0) * 0.5
            return round(float(collapse_score), 4)

    @torch.no_grad()
    def analyze_pos_neg_margin_with_category_breakdown(
        self,
        dataloader,
        num_batches: int = 10,
        eps: float = 0.5,
        topk_categories: int = 20,
    ):
        self.model.eval()

        margins_all = []
        low_pos_cat, low_neg_cat = Counter(), Counter()
        wrong_pos_cat, wrong_neg_cat = Counter(), Counter()
        low_total, wrong_total = 0, 0

        for step, batch in enumerate(dataloader):
            if step >= num_batches:
                break
            if not (isinstance(batch, (list, tuple)) and len(batch) >= 4):
                continue

            _, seq, pos, neg = batch[0], batch[1], batch[2], batch[3]

            seq_np = seq.cpu().numpy() if isinstance(seq, torch.Tensor) else seq
            log_feats = self.model.log2feats(seq_np)

            pos_t = torch.as_tensor(pos, device=self.device, dtype=torch.long)
            neg_t = torch.as_tensor(neg, device=self.device, dtype=torch.long)

            all_items = torch.stack([pos_t, neg_t], dim=-1)
            all_logits = self.model.predict_score(log_feats, all_items)
            margin = all_logits[..., 0] - all_logits[..., 1]

            # DEBUG: Match the training loss mask and exclude all padded targets.
            seq_t = torch.as_tensor(seq_np, device=self.device, dtype=torch.long)
            valid = (seq_t != 0) & (pos_t != 0) & (neg_t != 0)
            if valid.any():
                margins_all.append(margin[valid].detach().float().cpu())

            margin_cpu = margin.detach().float().cpu().numpy()
            pos_cpu = pos_t.detach().cpu().numpy()
            neg_cpu = neg_t.detach().cpu().numpy()
            valid_cpu = valid.detach().cpu().numpy()

            low_mask = valid_cpu & (margin_cpu < float(eps))
            wrong_mask = valid_cpu & (margin_cpu < 0.0)

            for b, l in np.argwhere(low_mask):
                low_total += 1
                pid = int(pos_cpu[b, l])
                nid = int(neg_cpu[b, l])
                for c in self._get_categories(pid):
                    low_pos_cat[c] += 1
                for c in self._get_categories(nid):
                    low_neg_cat[c] += 1

            for b, l in np.argwhere(wrong_mask):
                wrong_total += 1
                pid = int(pos_cpu[b, l])
                nid = int(neg_cpu[b, l])
                for c in self._get_categories(pid):
                    wrong_pos_cat[c] += 1
                for c in self._get_categories(nid):
                    wrong_neg_cat[c] += 1

        if len(margins_all) == 0:
            margin_metrics = {
                "mean": 0.0,
                "p10": 0.0,
                "neg_beats_pos_rate": 0.0,
                "small_margin_rate": 0.0,
            }
        else:
            m = torch.cat(margins_all, dim=0)
            N = m.numel()

            k = max(1, int(np.ceil(0.10 * N)))
            p10 = float(torch.kthvalue(m, k).values.item())

            margin_metrics = {
                "mean": round(float(m.mean().item()), 4),
                "p10": round(p10, 4),
                "neg_beats_pos_rate": round(float((m < 0.0).float().mean().item()), 4),
                "small_margin_rate": round(
                    float((m < float(eps)).float().mean().item()), 4
                ),
            }

        def _topk(counter: Counter, k: int):
            return [{"category": c, "count": int(n)} for c, n in counter.most_common(k)]

        breakdown = {
            # DEBUG: Distinguish unavailable category labels from measured counts.
            "category_breakdown_available": False,
            "category_breakdown_unavailable_reason": (
                "Item categories are not provided by this benchmark."
            ),
            "valid_positions": sum(int(m.numel()) for m in margins_all),
            "eps": float(eps),
            "low_margin_total_positions": int(low_total),
            "wrong_rank_total_positions": int(wrong_total),
            "low_margin_top_categories": {
                "pos_item": _topk(low_pos_cat, topk_categories),
                "neg_item": _topk(low_neg_cat, topk_categories),
            },
            "wrong_rank_top_categories": {
                "pos_item": _topk(wrong_pos_cat, topk_categories),
                "neg_item": _topk(wrong_neg_cat, topk_categories),
            },
        }

        return margin_metrics, breakdown

    def run_full_diagnosis(self, train_loader):
        print(">>> Running Simplified Diagnosis (no SVD, no shuffle)...")

        collapse_score = self.analyze_embeddings_collapse_cosine(sample_size=2048)
        eps = 0.5
        margin_metrics, breakdown = self.analyze_pos_neg_margin_with_category_breakdown(
            train_loader, num_batches=10, eps=eps, topk_categories=20
        )
        return {
            "metrics": {
                "embedding_collapse_score": collapse_score,
                "pos_neg_margin_mean": margin_metrics["mean"],
                "pos_neg_margin_p10": margin_metrics["p10"],
                "pos_neg_neg_beats_pos_rate": margin_metrics["neg_beats_pos_rate"],
                "pos_neg_small_margin_rate": margin_metrics["small_margin_rate"],
                "pos_neg_margin_category_breakdown": breakdown,
            },
            "metric_definitions": {
                "embedding_collapse_score": (
                    "Range ~[0,1]. Estimated by mean pairwise cosine similarity of sampled item embeddings "
                    "(mapped to [0,1]). Higher means embeddings point in similar directions (worse diversity / more collapse)."
                ),
                "pos_neg_margin_mean": "Mean of (pos_logit - neg_logit) over valid positions; higher means clearer separation.",
                "pos_neg_margin_p10": "10th percentile of (pos_logit - neg_logit); lower suggests many hard/confusing cases.",
                "pos_neg_neg_beats_pos_rate": "Fraction where neg_logit > pos_logit (margin < 0); lower is better.",
                "pos_neg_small_margin_rate": "Fraction where (pos_logit - neg_logit) < eps; higher means weak separation.",
                # DEBUG: Describe measured counts without claiming unavailable metadata.
                "pos_neg_margin_category_breakdown": (
                    "Reports valid training-position counts and counts of low-margin "
                    "(margin<eps) and wrong-rank (margin<0) cases. Category breakdowns "
                    "are unavailable because item category labels are not provided; "
                    "empty category lists are not measured zero category counts. "
                    "If valid_positions is zero, margin summary values are placeholders "
                    "and must not be interpreted as measured separation."
                ),
            },
        }
